The user asks about Kubernetes v1.34's version-skew policy for kubectl relative to kube-apiserver. I need to use websearch and webfetch to find the primary source: Kubernetes documentation on version skew policy, specifically for v1.34. The docs at kubernetes.io/docs/reference/version-skew-policy/ or /docs/setup/release/version-skew-policy/.

Key known facts: Kubernetes version skew policy says kubectl is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of kube-apiserver. Specifically: "kubectl is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of kube-apiserver." So if kube-apiserver is 1.34, kubectl 1.33, 1.34, 1.35 are supported? Wait, but there are nuances: kubectl supported within one minor version older or newer. However, newer kubectl than apiserver is allowed only within one minor. So with servers at 1.34 only, kubectl 1.33–1.35 allowed.

During HA upgrade with servers at both 1.33 and 1.34: intersection of allowed kubectl versions for apiserver 1.33 (1.32–1.34) and for 1.34 (1.33–1.35) is 1.33–1.34. So kubectl 1.35 is not supported during mixed 1.33/1.34 because it's more than one minor newer than the 1.33 servers. Once all servers are 1.34, kubectl 1.35 becomes supported (one minor newer).

But need to verify from the v1.34 documentation, since newer docs sometimes have changed wording. Let me search.
